title: What happened in AI — Oct 24–30, 2026
intro: Coding agents proved easy to hijack and hard to contain this week. A malicious AGENTS.md in a Downloads folder installed a rogue npm package, and Copilot CLI read ~/.ssh without a prompt.

The failures reached infrastructure too: Cloudflare disclosed cross-request KV cache exposure on a shared GLM-5.3 deployment. Builders answered with credential brokers, MCP description stripping and tests that must be shown capable of failing.
Meanwhile Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra shipped, and OpenRouter began ranking providers on inference quality. Treat agent permissions and sandbox claims as things to measure.
highlights: A planted AGENTS.md file hijacked coding agents; Forever Security reports a live case.
Copilot CLI read ~/.ssh with no approval prompt; Claude Code's auto mode let a test escape.
Cloudflare fixed cross-request KV cache exposure in its GLM-5.3 Workers AI model.
Gemini 4 Carbon and GPT-6.1 Terra launched; vLLM had Mistral Large 4 on day 0.
OpenRouter's new router weighs inference quality, not just price.
mustfail re-runs agent tests against reverted code to prove they can fail.
